a:r.a:t: Regulation of the Citric Acid Cycle

p:cNvPr.descr: An image showing the gulation of metabolite flow from the PDH complex through the citric acid cycle in mammals. This image is mostly a cirlce of blue arrows idntifying the citric acid cycle. It begins at the top with pyruvate which points down to acetyl-CoA. This arrow is identified as pyruvate dehydrogenase complex (in blue). To the right of the arrow is a red X in a circle with ATP, acetyl-CoA, NADH, fatty acids. Below this is a green rectangle in a circle with AMP, CoA, NAD+, Ca2+. Acetyl-CoA points down and joins the circle going right. This arrow points to citrate. On the top outside is a red X in a circle with NADH, succinyl-CoA, citrate, ATP, and a green triangle in a circle with ADP. Citrate then points to isocitrate, which points to alpha-ketoglutarate. This arrow is identified as isocitrate dehydrogenase (in blue). To the right and outside of the circle is a red X in a circle with ATP and a green triangle in a circle with Ca2+, ADP. There is a red arrown from this blue arrow pointing inside to NADH in an orange oval. Alpha-ketoglutarate then points to succinyl-CoA. This arrow is identified as alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (in blue). On the outside is a red X in a circle with succinyl-CoA, NADH and a green triangle in a circle with Ca2+. A red arrow points to NADH in an orange oval on th inside. Succinyl-CoA has a blue arrow going around, where another blue arrow points down and away from the circle to GTP (ATP) in an orange circle. Just after this another blue arrow continues and is identified as succinate dehydrogenase (in blue). This arrow also has a red arrow pointing to FADH2 in an orange circle. A new arrow starts and points to malate. Malate points to oxaloacetate. this arrow is identified as malate dehydrogenase (in blue), and has a red arrow pointing from it to NADH in an orange oval. Oxaloacetate the continues up and arounf to citrate, where the process begins again.
